title: Honest Interval Length for Rare-Event Effects under Two-Sided Independent Adjudication
banked_reason: D-0.5 REJECT/NO-PASS: the flagship kernel is repository-subsumed by stat_rare_adjudication_translation_ci; signed aggregation removes any four-channel decision frontier.
gap_reasons: Pivot before Stage 0: the flagship kernel is repository-subsumed by stat_rare_adjudication_translation_ci, and the two-sided extension must create a non-aggregable decision problem plus a credible deployment condition to meet the field floor.
The predecessor's full-record mixed-limit theorem already contains the claimed kernel; the extra two error channels are admitted here to aggregate away rather than creating a new information regime.
The central OEQ is the predecessor's explicit unresolved unknown-center count-using attainment obligation with only a two-sided relabelling of nuisance coordinates.

The load-bearing conditional error bound U/sqrt(n) requires reporting accuracy to improve deterministically with each row size; its justification calls it a deployment boundary but supplies no mechanism or real setting satisfying that triangular condition.
proof_attempt_summary: The literature scout harvested three open problems, and one proto-core proposal was authored and independently reviewed. D-0.5 rejected all five headline/OEQ kernels as repository-subsumed after signed aggregation reduced the two-sided extension to the predecessor count game; two orchestrator consultations confirmed no faithful bounded field-tier repair. No derivation or Lean proof was attempted; the unknown-center selector remains predecessor debt rather than a new field-level proposal.
tldr: The missing result in the downgraded one-sided rare-adjudication proposal is unknown-center attainment of its count-using interval value. For two-sided independent audits, four discordance channels reduce in the limit minimax problem to two signed Poisson totals. The substantive target is a matched all-procedure expanding-local expected-length theorem: one observed-data connected interval has at least \(90\%\) coverage at every admissible finite row and attains the Gaussian--Poisson value uniformly over unknown interior reported risks. A terminating outward-certified center library must preserve coverage and expected length at zero intensities. A fresh balanced witness demonstrates a strict benefit from using counts, while leaving the full value and the uniform construction open.
gap: The closest internal predecessor failed to transfer its count-using decision value to one exactly honest unknown-center interval. Published decaying-label normal theory and minimax confidence-region computation do not discharge that obligation.
fill: The kernel matches the full observed-data lower bound to a single certified pilot-selected interval. The numerical hierarchy is uniform in the center and includes zero-intensity faces; sign aggregation is credited as a reduction rather than as four-dimensional novelty.
